title: the
note: Spanish has TWO words for 'the' — and there's a real reason why.

because.title: Why two words for "the"?
because.explain: Latin sorted every noun into THREE bins — masculine, feminine and neuter. The names are just labels; it has nothing to do with boy/girl. Think electrical plugs: Type A, Type B, Type C. Spanish lost the third bin. Most neuter words slid into the "el" pile — which is why "nombre" and "vino", both neuter in Latin, are "el" words today.
because.key: Cheat code: a word ending in -o goes in the "el" bin, a word ending in -a goes in the "la" bin. That covers most words you'll meet. Words ending in anything else — "café", for one — the rule simply doesn't decide; you pick those up as you go.
because.fun: English had all three bins too, and lost them between roughly 1000 and 1400. Vikings are part of the story: Norse and English speakers muddling through each other's word endings helped wear them away.
because.src: The real term is "grammatical gender." Linguists call it "noun class."
